targets.claim: The French prosecutor leading the investigation into the Germanwings Flight 9525 crash denied knowledge of any video footage from the plane.
There were reports of a cell phone video showing the final moments before the crash.
The video is said to show passengers screaming and metallic banging sounds, possibly from the pilot trying to open the cockpit door.
The crash killed all 150 people on board.
The co-pilot, Andreas Lubitz, has been found to have had a history of depression and suicidal tendencies.
Investigators are looking into whether Lubitz deliberately brought down the plane.
Recovery efforts are ongoing and personal belongings of the victims, including cell phones, are being collected/recovered.

claims.quote: The French prosecutor leading the investigation into the Germanwings Flight 9525 crash has denied knowledge of any video footage from the plane
claims.reason: Marseille prosecutor Brice Robin told CNN he was not aware of any video footage from on board the plane.
claims.evidence_quote: The French prosecutor leading an investigation into the crash of Germanwings Flight 9525 insisted Wednesday that he was not aware of any video footage from on board the plane.

claims.quote: despite reports of a cell phone video showing the final moments before the crash
claims.reason: Two magazines, Bild and Paris Match, reported a cell phone video showing the harrowing final seconds from on board the plane.
claims.evidence_quote: claims by two magazines, German daily Bild and French Paris Match, of a cell phone video showing the harrowing final seconds from on board Germanwings Flight 9525 as it crashed into the French Alps.

claims.quote: The video is said to show passengers screaming and metallic banging sounds, possibly from the pilot trying to open the cockpit door
claims.reason: Paris Match reported cries of 'My God' in several languages and metallic banging, possibly from the pilot trying to open the cockpit door with a heavy object.
claims.evidence_quote: "One can hear cries of 'My God' in several languages," Paris Match reported. "Metallic banging can also be heard more than three times, perhaps of the pilot trying to open the cockpit door with a heavy object."
